name: netudp
description: UDP on the kernel's network stack (net-mux S3): with the network modules loaded, every AF_INET datagram socket is a 2.11BSD struct socket reached through net.mod's descriptor.  loopprobe -u runs its cases over lo0 -- a datagram both ways with the sender named, bind to port 0, a connected socket hearing only its peer, select and FIONREAD, a blocked select woken by a child's datagram, FIONBIO and MSG_DONTWAIT answering EAGAIN, EADDRINUSE and SO_REUSEADDR, MSG_OOB refused, EBADF on a closed descriptor -- and prints UDP OK only when none failed.  A case that blocks forever shows as the frame cap.  The harness has no network card, so lo0 is the only interface.  First syslogd is restarted with -u and loopprobe -s sends it a user.err line over lo0, which syslog.conf sends to the console: `syslogd ok' is the line's tail, which nothing but its arrival can print.  The network modules are loaded at boot (/etc/rc).  Last, /etc/resolv.conf names 127.0.0.1 and loopprobe -h asks gethostbyname for a name while a child bound to port 53 answers with a junk datagram every second for 12 s: the resolver must give up on its own deadline, three 1.5 s tries, and `DNS OK' says it returned within 7 s.
